name: NumberRange
simple: A NumberRange is a pair of numbers: a smallest (Min) and a biggest (Max). Roblox picks random numbers between them. It is mostly used in ParticleEmitters, like how long each particle lives or how fast it flies.
analogy: It is like saying "bring between 3 and 5 friends". Each time, the number could be anything from 3 to 5.
whenToUse: ParticleEmitter.Lifetime: how many seconds each particle lasts
ParticleEmitter.Speed: how fast particles shoot out
ParticleEmitter.Rotation and RotSpeed: how much particles spin
Storing any "from this to that" range in your own code
where: Works in any script. Make one with NumberRange.new(min, max) or NumberRange.new(value).

terms.range: All the numbers from a smallest to a biggest. The range 2 to 5 includes 2, 3.7, 5, and so on.
terms.Min: The smallest number in the range.
terms.Max: The biggest number in the range.
terms.ParticleEmitter: An object that shoots out lots of little images (particles) to make fire, smoke, sparkles, and similar effects.
terms.32-bit float: The way NumberRange stores numbers. It keeps about 7 digits of accuracy, so very big or very precise numbers get rounded a little.

examples.title: Sparkles that live a random amount of time
examples.code:
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
part.Parent = workspace

local emitter = Instance.new("ParticleEmitter")
emitter.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(1, 3) -- each particle lives 1 to 3 seconds
emitter.Speed = NumberRange.new(5)       -- every particle moves at exactly 5
emitter.Parent = part
explain: NumberRange.new(1, 3): each particle gets a random lifetime between 1 and 3 seconds, so they do not all vanish at once.
NumberRange.new(5): Min and Max are both 5, so every particle has the same speed.
Putting the emitter inside the part makes the sparkles come out of the part.

gotchas: Min must be smaller than or equal to Max. NumberRange.new(5, 1) causes an error.
You cannot change .Min or .Max after making it. Make a new NumberRange instead.

NumberRange.new.simple: Makes a NumberRange. Give it one number to make Min and Max the same, or two numbers for Min and Max.
NumberRange.new.example:
local exact = NumberRange.new(2)      -- Min 2, Max 2
local between = NumberRange.new(1, 4) -- Min 1, Max 4
print(between.Min, between.Max) --> 1 4
NumberRange.new.gotcha: The first number must not be bigger than the second.

NumberRange.Min.simple: The smallest number in the range. Always less than or equal to Max.

NumberRange.Max.simple: The biggest number in the range. Always greater than or equal to Min.
